why.rules.geometry: 3.12.6 (owner: «там что, опять одни и те же фигуры… если это одно и то же повторяется каждую игру, даже если оно перемешивается, это вообще не годится»): every figure is made anew for every game (games/geometry-model.js generateFigures). Until then a level had a fixed pool — 12 / 14 / 15 figures, 3 / 4 / 5 a game — dealt in rounds, so the same figures came back every 3–4 games. kinds: the kinds of figure of a level with their weights — Easy: triangles and symmetric quadrilaterals with sides along the grid (rectangle, isosceles trapezoid, parallelogram, kite), as the pool of 3.12.1; Medium: irregular quadrilaterals, convex or an arrowhead (dart); Hard: 5–8 vertices — convex pentagons and hexagons, L-shapes, boxes with two notches (T, U, steps), figures with one or two inward vertices, a four-pointed star. grid: the vertices sit on the crossings of the grid (Easy and Medium) or of half cells (Hard). min_edge: the shortest edge, in hundredths of the field. per_game: how many figures of one kind a game may have. Every figure is a simple polygon inside the field with no angle under 25°, none within 20° of a straight line, no vertex closer than 6 to another edge, a box of at least 30 × 30, and not like another figure of the same game. The 11-vertex tree and the 10-vertex star of the old Hard pool are gone: the model average player drew them mostly Very Bad. The pools of the original (geometry_fig_d0..2) are no longer read.
why.MG_geometry_easy.level_up_param: 3.12.6 (the figures are made anew for every game, see rules.geometry): up 4000 → 3500 — a Good and two Bad, or better. Random triangles and quadrilaterals are harder to keep in mind than the hand-made pool was: at 4000 the novice passed 47 % of the games. Now novice 63 %, average 97 %, strong 100 %. 3.12.5 (the accuracy is the places of the vertices, see geometry_results_data): up 6000 → 4000 — two Good and one Bad, or better. Novice 64 % of the games, average 98 %, strong 100 %; 6000 (three Very Good) would pass 5 % of the novice's games. With the stretch and the turn of the model players half as big the novice passes about 80 %, one and a half times as big about 45 %. Before: 3.12.1 (owner: Easy has to be simple, Medium harder, Hard harder still): up 6500 → 6000 ({VG, VG, VG} or better). The new Easy pool has no near-copies of the easiest triangles (the near-equilateral one and the right isosceles one were each there twice), and at 6500 the model average player passed 85 % of the games (novice 55 %); at 6000 — 99 % (novice 86 %), 3 games for 3 steps. Scores go in steps of 500, so there is nothing between. Before: Easy asks 93 % of the maximum ({P, P, P} or {P, P, VG}) and is the strictest step: with the doc's noise model (tools/analysis/train_balance_geometry.mjs, real figures and comparison, σ = 6 / 4 / 2 % of the field) novice 29 %, average 62 %, strong 98 % (Medium: 13 / 48 / 97 %). up 6500 ({P, VG, VG} or {P, P, G}, 87 % of the maximum like Medium 83 % and Hard 87.5 %): novice 68 %, average 92 % (3 games for 3 steps), strong 100 %; the same with the memory-load variant. Unlock (4th number): level-ups needed to open the game. v3.3 (owner: the last games opened too slowly): 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 instead of 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 16, 18 — the average model player opens all 12 games in 23–30 trainings instead of 30–42 (tools/analysis/unlock_pace.py).

why.MG_geometry_hard.level_up_param: 3.12.6 (the figures are made anew for every game, see rules.geometry): up 13500 → 13000. Figures of 5–8 vertices instead of the pool with the 11-vertex tree; the hardest kinds are the four-pointed star, the 7-vertex figures with two inward vertices and the boxes with two notches (the average player draws them Very Bad in 38–56 % of the rounds, a pentagon in 9 %). Average 24 % of the games, strong 94 %, novice 0 %. 3.12.5 (the accuracy is the places of the vertices, see geometry_results_data): up 16500 → 13500 — two Good and three Bad, or better. Average 26 % of the games, strong 93 %, novice 0 %. The 11-vertex tree and the 10-vertex star are the hardest figures: the average player draws them mostly Very Bad; the pool is dealt in rounds, so one game in three has the tree. Before: owner: hard was practically impossible — up 17500 passed 3 % of the games of the model average player with memory load (15 % in the doc's model), 283 games for the 10 steps. With 15 s and the three replaced figures up 16500 (e.g. three Very Good and two Good, or four Very Good and one Bad) gives: average 27 % (doc's model 57 %), strong 97 % (100 %), novice 1 % (5 %); weak games (< 6600): average 1 %, novice 24 %; 36 games for the 10 steps of the average player. The two player models bracket the truth; the fit follows the one with memory load because it reproduces the owner's experience. Mean scores of the average player rise 6865 / 9391 / 14225 (x1.37, x1.51). Easy (6500: average 92 %, novice 68 %) and medium (10000: average 49 %, novice 13 %) stay: scores move in steps of 500, the next easy threshold (7000) would drop the average player to 62 %.
why.geometry_game_field.diff_max_time: Content ladder: easy = 3 triangles, medium = 4 quadrilaterals, hard = 5 figures of 4-11 vertices — and all three give the same 10 s to memorise. Hard gets 15 s (1.4-3.8 s a vertex, like the 2.5-3.3 s of easy and medium). In the player model with memory load (tools/analysis/train_balance_geometry.mjs: vertex noise sigma 6 / 4 / 2 % of the field, growing with the vertices per memorising time) the mean hard score of the average player goes 13092 -> 14225 together with the figure changes below.
why.geometry_results_data: 3.12.3 (owner: a copy that looks very much like the original gets a number nobody can explain; the logic of the estimate has to be understood and corrected). The number of the original is the share of the tolerance of the level that is left (60 / 30 / 20 % of the angle sum), so one and the same drawing read differently on every level: a hexagon with 63° of angle differences in all was 86 % on Easy, 71 % on Medium and 57 % on Hard. The game now shows 100 minus the sum of the angle differences in percent of the angle sum — one scale for every level (that hexagon: 91 %), and the bands say how strict a level is. The limits are the bands of the original (10 / 25 / 50 / 85 % of the tolerance) moved to the new scale: Bad, Good, Very Good, Perfect start at 46 / 55 / 70 / 91 % on Easy, 73 / 77 / 85 / 95 % on Medium and 82 / 85 / 90 / 97 % on Hard. Easy and Hard are exactly as before; on Medium two limits fell between whole percents (77.5 and 95.5) and were rounded down, in the player's favour. max_fig_diff_miss_percent is no longer read. 3.12.4 (owner: Easy is won often by a beginner, but not every time): Very Good on Easy starts at 78 % instead of 70 %, so the ladder of Very Good is 78 / 85 / 90 %. The step of Easy (6000, three Very Good) passed 87 % of the novice's games (target 60–75 %), and the points go by 500, so the threshold itself could not be set between 6000 and 6500 (6500: novice 55 %, average 85 %). With 78 %: novice 74 %, average 96 %, strong 100 % (memory model of tools/analysis/train_balance_geometry.mjs). 3.12.5 (owner: «совсем неточная фигура, а пишет 90 с чем-то процентов» — the logic of the estimate has to be reviewed and corrected on every level): the angles alone do not see the proportions, the tilt or a vertex in the wrong place whose angle stays — a copy 30 % too wide kept 95–96 %. The accuracy is now how close the vertices of the copy are to their places once it is moved and scaled onto the original (games/geometry-model.js figureMatch): 100 − 200 × the root mean square distance in radii of the figure — that copy 30 % too wide is 74 %, a copy turned by 5° is 82 %. The band limits are set anew on this scale, a little stricter on every level up: Bad, Good, Very Good, Perfect from 40 / 55 / 70 / 85 % on Easy, 45 / 60 / 75 / 88 % on Medium and 50 / 65 / 80 / 92 % on Hard, and the thresholds follow (MG_geometry_*). The model players (tools/analysis/train_balance_geometry.mjs) also stretch and turn the whole copy now [assumption, from real copies].
